PHP86-014.area: Assignment/reference/list-derived dimension and property writes, read-modify-write, unset and reference fetch; nested and discarded contexts.
PHP86-014.mechanismEvidence: Ordinary assignment emits TMP; nonreference list RHS is TMP or CONST. RC4 var dispatch admits those into write consumers whose VM operand declarations exclude TMP/CONST. Ten executed probes report matching invalid opcode tuples. No opcode dump or exact-pin build was used.
PHP86-014.known: Assignment reads and existing call-result writes succeed. PHP86-004 constant-object property mutation is independently supported. Literal temporary/constant-array-only/nullsafe writes reject. RC4 reference-result writes and reference-bearing list writes succeed in the tested processes, without establishing language intent.
PHP86-014.unknown: Whether assignment-derived write forms should be rejected or supported, including successful reference-result forms; final upstream repair and all VM profiles.
PHP86-014.grammarRisk: No missing structural form established; both grammars already accept the affected dereference structure. A premature contextual rule could wrongly accept or reject; runtime invalid opcode must not be encoded as syntax rejection.
PHP86-014.certificationImpact: Blocks affected-area correctness and candidate/stable certification. Does not block independent evidence work.
PHP86-014.closureEvidence: Authoritative exact-form intended-validity disposition, coherent compiler/VM implementation, exact-pin and final-release execution, operation/result-kind and live/discarded regressions.
PHP86-014.requiredSpecificationChange: No normative change established; C5C-D02 proposes research-scope clarification only.

PHP86-015.area: Optimized printf/sprintf format traversal, ordinary/dynamic/namespace/named/unpack calls, arrays, constant closures and related PFA eligibility.
PHP86-015.known: Specialization attempts constant evaluation before checking format eligibility. AND/OR visit both children; known ternary/coalesce discard untaken nodes. Named/unpack gates bypass specialization; literal arrays may independently enter constant evaluation. Ordinary PFA and constant PFA bound arguments use different traversals.
PHP86-015.unknown: Intended compatibility boundary and comprehensive dispatch/optimization interactions; whether upstream regards exact discarded-cast differences as defects.
PHP86-015.grammarRisk: No structural change; function-specific EBNF would misrepresent the mechanism. Universal argument-traversal prose is unsupported.
PHP86-015.certificationImpact: Blocks complete contextual-traversal correctness and candidate/stable claims.
PHP86-015.closureEvidence: Authoritative compatibility disposition, stage-aware source-corresponding regression tests and complete reviewed dispatch scope.
PHP86-015.requiredSpecificationChange: C5C-D01 documentation clarification proposed; no new normative generalization authorized. Existing visited-AST clauses and historical statement table remain accurate within scope.

CA86-001.area: Inherited hook-name EBNF restriction in discarded declarations.
CA86-001.known: 8.5 and RC4 parser accepts identifier; compiler rejects unknown hook only when declaration visited. Both repository grammars intentionally restrict hook-name to get/set even when discarded; historical specification states this explicitly.
CA86-001.unknown: No unanswered mechanism question for tested live/retained/discarded/get controls; future policy choice is separate.
CA86-001.grammarRisk: Known intentional false rejection relative to unrestricted Zend-acceptance equivalence, not new RC4 syntax.
CA86-001.certificationImpact: Must retain explicit narrowed claim; unrestricted acceptance-equivalence cannot be certified with this difference.
CA86-001.closureEvidence: Classification complete; a policy reversal requires separate historical-correction governance and Gate B implementation evidence.
